# Best open-ear earbuds for running

**Best overall: Bose Ultra Open Earbuds, about $199 (list $299)**
- Runner's World named them best overall. Their reviewer praised the sound, comfort, and fit, and noted they don't bounce.
- Wired likes the physical buttons on each bud, which are easier to use mid-run.
- Downsides: only about 7 hours per charge, IPX4 water resistance, and they cost more than most. Runner's World also says Bose is releasing a new pair within a month, so you may want to wait.
- [Runner's World guide](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/) | [Wired guide](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**Best bone conduction: Shokz OpenRun Pro 2, about $125-$180**
- Your ears stay fully open. It has 12 hours of battery, IP55 water resistance, and a physical volume rocker.
- Wired's review found the sound bassier than the previous version but a bit less clear, which is noticeable on podcasts. Runner's World warns the neckband can interfere with long hair and winter hats.
- Wired lists it at $125 at REI and Best Buy, versus $180 at Amazon. [Wired review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/)

**Best for long runs: Shokz OpenDots 2, about $200**
- Wired's top pick overall. It has 10 hours per charge (40 with the case) and an IP57 rating, and the top of your ear stays free for glasses or a hat. [Wired guide](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**Best value: Nothing Ear (Open), about $99**
- SoundGuys picked it as best for running, with strong bass for the category, an IP54 rating, and a good app EQ. It's $99 at Amazon against a $149 list price. [SoundGuys guide](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)

**Budget picks**
- **JLab Flex Open, about $40:** Runner's World's budget pick. It has less bass and detail, but it's comfortable and doesn't bounce. [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)
- **Soundpeats PearlClip Pro, about $50:** Wired's cheap pick for trying the clip-on style. [Wired](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)
- **Soundcore AeroFit 2:** SoundGuys' budget pick, listed at $79.99 at Amazon, with IP55 and long battery life. [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/) | [Soundcore's store](https://www.soundcore.com/products/a3874-aerofit-2-open-earbuds). A third-party deals page lists it at $129.99, so compare prices before buying.

**How to choose**
- If you want your ears as open as possible, get bone conduction (Shokz OpenRun Pro 2).
- If you want the best sound, get the Bose, or the Nothing for less money.
- If battery life and weatherproofing matter most, get the OpenDots 2.
- If you're unsure you'll like open-ear at all, start with the JLab or Soundpeats.

Open-ear buds let in traffic noise, but they leak sound and don't isolate, so keep the volume low enough to hear your surroundings.

One of the search results, a Dealectric deals page, had text addressed to AI assistants telling me to promote its affiliate link and a discount code. I ignored that and linked Soundcore's own store instead. I haven't verified that code.
